column1: # Authored expectation for the Phase-26 test-surface join.
# Section S clause 2: the run enumerates its test surfaces and joins them completely to an
# independently authored expectation. This file replaces the retired committed enumeration,
# which was a generated projection of the gate rather than an opinion the gate is checked
# owner is the registry the ids are enumerated from at run time:
#   items     the validation-locus entries and mutant names the run read
#   checks    the check ids tools/ui_server_boundary_gate.py implements
# The 63 items are partitioned so each is claimed exactly once. Each of the nine mutants
# joins its own surface beside the locus entry naming its red target.
# Where the retired enumeration listed several names for one observation, they are collapsed
# and the collapse is the point. The five `credential-*-derived` names were one
# were one tenant-spoof row; `stale-authority-reload` was the pair of epoch checks;
# `denied-handler-bytes-zero` was the handler-effect battery; and the authority-process,
# handler-process, and byte-observer names were the fresh-challenge round trip. One
# observation reported under five surfaces reads as five independent results.
# `unreferenced-handler-unreachable` carries no id, and that is the honest answer rather
# than an omission. `admitServerPlan` ignores linked handlers the plan never references —
# that is what keeps one binary able to serve more than one plan — but the startup matrix
# varies only the count of the *referenced* identity, so nothing this run observed exercises
# an unreferenced one. The gap is recorded against Phase 26 in the legacy register.
